snippet.title: Islands of New Zealand: The Huhu Beetle
snippet.description:
The huhu beetle is a longhorn beetle endemic to New Zealand, reaching up to 5 cm in length. It is one of the largest beetles in the country, found across the nation. As an adult, it cannot eat, relying on its larval stage for survival. The larva can grow to 5 to 7 cm, living in dead wood and feeding on gymnosperms. It is high in protein and fat, making it a food source for some New Zealanders. Its life cycle and habitat reflect unique ecological adaptations to New Zealand’s environment. The beetle has a long history in New Zealand, with cultural and ecological significance.
